svg.title: 4. Time-series storage by query pattern
svg.text: Managed Service for Apache Flink: one application, three operators
Pick the store by the question
Time-series storage: one stream, four stores, each chosen by the question it answers (EU numbers, 600,000 devices)
1 item per device-day of rollups, 2 years
"Is my heat pump on, and how warm is it?"
"Show me last week, minute by minute."
Athena over Iceberg, partition-pruned by day
1.2 KB per message = 2.4 MB/s, about 207 GB/day as JSON
Kinesis: 3 shards by throughput, 8 to drain backlogs
about 4 KB each, about 5 TB at 90 days
InfluxDB: series = dimensions you group by,
not devices. 600,000 device tags would be 7.2M series
Iceberg: Parquet + ZSTD is usually several times
smaller than the JSON; measure with your payloads
Why not put every sample in a time-series database? Because the per-device question is a key lookup,
and a tag per device turns 12 fields into millions of series. Keep the TSDB for the questions it is good at.
